voice.text: You drink a cup of water. [pause] Where did that water come from? Tap your guess.
Everything we use comes from the <emphasis>Earth</emphasis>. [pause] Water from rain and rivers. [pause] Wood from trees. [pause] Food from plants.

When we are done with a thing, we <emphasis>choose</emphasis>: trash, reuse, or recycle. [pause] The trash truck takes trash to a landfill on the land — it does <emphasis>not</emphasis> disappear. [pause] Reuse means: use it again! [pause] Recycle means: make it into something new.
Our choices touch the water, the land, the air, and the animals. [pause] A clean stream is full of life. [pause] A littered stream is empty. [pause] Every choice matters — even one wrapper.
Drag each thing to trash, reuse, or recycle. [pause] Or tap a button. [pause] Then help the stream!
Trash, reuse, or recycle?
Yes! [pause] It's not broken — wash it and use it again. It can hold crayons!
Yes! [pause] Paper can be made into new paper.
Yes! [pause] Food scraps go to trash or compost — not the recycle bin.
Yes! [pause] Plastic can be made into something new.
Yes! [pause] It makes a great cleaning rag — used again!
Yes! [pause] Too sticky and small to recycle. Into the trash — never on the ground.
Not quite. [pause] Recycling melts things into something new. This one isn't done yet — use the same one again. Reuse!
Not quite. [pause] It's all used up as it is — but it can be made into something new. Recycle!
Wait! [pause] Trash sits in the landfill forever. This one can have a second life.
Not quite. [pause] Food scraps can't become new paper or bottles. Trash or compost for this one.
All sorted! [pause] Now help the stream. Tap the choice that helps.
A candy wrapper is in your hand at the stream. What helps the stream? [pause] Keep it in your pocket until you find a trash can, [pause] or drop it — one little wrapper doesn't matter?
You find a plastic bottle by the stream. What helps? [pause] Toss it in the water — the water will take it away, [pause] or take it home to the recycle bin?
Yes! [pause] Every wrapper you hold onto keeps the stream clean for the fish.
Yes! [pause] Now it becomes something new — and the stream stays clean.
Not quite. [pause] The stream animals feel every wrapper. One person's choice matters!
Not quite. [pause] The water can't make it disappear — it just carries the trash to the animals.
The stream is clean, thanks to you! [pause] Now show what you know.
The trash truck drives away. Where does the trash go? [pause] To a landfill — a big pile on the land, [pause] or, it disappears forever?
What does reuse mean? [pause] Use the same thing again, [pause] or melt it down into something new — same as recycling?
Paper goes in the recycle bin. What happens to it? [pause] It is made into new paper, [pause] or it is used again as the very same sheet?
One kid picks up one wrapper by the stream. Does it help? [pause] Yes — every choice helps the water and the animals, [pause] or, no — one person can't change anything?
Where does the wood in your chair come from? [pause] Trees that grew on the Earth, [pause] or, the store makes it out of nothing?
<soft>You are an Earth helper!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the Earth and the bins once more.
Lesson done! Go find three things at home to reuse, with your parent. Then draw them in your journal.
